messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: [prod-inference] 5 crashloop restarts on deployment=serve-vllm-model-a in rwd-prd-1 (gpu nodes). Severity: potential customer impact. Auto-paging oncall-sre and oncall-ml.

alex: seeing this, paging now. Which model, any pattern? @jess are you on ml oncall?

jess: oncall-ml here. Crashloops started ~03:23 UTC. Pods show SIGSEGV in runtime main loop. Flipping into logs:
```
[2026-03-15T03:23:18Z] runtime ERROR: segfault at 0x0 in kernel attention.cu:kv_cache_init+0x4f
[2026-03-15T03:23:18Z] runtime ERROR: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure (cudaErrorUnknown)
[2026-03-15T03:23:18Z] kernel: backtrace: 0x7f8a1... 0x7f8b2...
```

kevin: reproduces locally on a q2-8 GPU image with TensorRT kernels enabled. Suspect custom attention kernel in vLLM branch using fused attention. If driver calls fail, segfault propagates.

maria: circulate quick mitigation: scale deployment down to 0 to stop crash churn and reduce node flaps? We can reroute traffic to model-b (quantized fallback).

alex: agreed. Taking action: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/serve-vllm-model-a --replicas=0` and cordon node rwd-prd-1-azb-03 (possible bad GPU). Doing now.

incident-bot: ACTION LOG: alex scaled serve-vllm-model-a to 0 replicas. cordoned node rwd-prd-1-azb-03. Notifying cust-success.

raj: thanks. I'll start triage for impacted customers and draft a message. Which customers hit 502s?

jess: Initial router logs show ~120 errors in last 10m, mostly from enterprise customers A and C. No data plane leakage but responses returned 502/503.

kevin: For debugging capture: please collect core and GPU driver logs from one crash pod before deleting. Run:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods | grep serve-vllm-model-a
kubectl -n inference logs <pod> -c runtime --previous
kubectl -n inference exec <node> -- journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n 200 > /tmp/nvidia-journal.log
scp node:/var/crash/core.<pid> s3://rwd-incident-dumps/1769823456/
```

maria: captured core dump and previous logs uploaded to s3://rwd-incident-dumps/1769823456/core.tgz

alex: good. Next step: roll a canary with runtime build 2026-03-12 (older kernels) and with TensorRT disabled. jess, can you prepare a canary image?

jess: building canary now with ENV DISABLE_TRT=1 and `vllm_runtime=v0.9.1-fix-kv`. Pushing -> will deploy 1 pod as canary.

incident-bot: DEPLOY: canary serve-vllm-model-a-canary created (1 pod) in inference namespace.

kevin: also check GPU driver version on node: `nvidia-smi` showed 525.85. Attempting local reproduce with same driver.

jess: canary pod up, logs show no segfault for 12 minutes. initial perf is slower ~1.8x but stable. Rolling a partial traffic shift: 90% to fallback model-b, 10% to canary for validation.

alex: implemented routing: set route weights: model-a -> 0% (scaled 0), model-a-canary -> 10%, model-b -> 90%. Monitor for errors.

raj: I'll send customers A and C a PS update: "We observed a runtime crash in our inference engine; we've rerouted traffic and are mitigating; investigations ongoing; will follow up." Keep me posted on ETA to restore full capacity.

maria: I pushed a defensive null-check in kv cache init to master; unit tests pass. Still need deeper kernel repro.

kevin: got a local coredump analyzed: null pointer in workspace allocation when sequence length spike > 8192. Kernel didn't handle unexpected seq_len. I'll open PR to add guard and fallback to CPU path for large seq.

jess: recommend backport hotfix to canary and then patch release. For now keep fallback routing in place and keep model-a scaled to 0. Continue collecting metrics.

alex: handing incident to jess for next shift. I'm out for 20m. jess, you're primary. Use channel for live updates. I'll remain reachable.

jess: taking over. Next steps: merge hotfix PR, run canary with patched runtime; if stable after 30m, ramp traffic 10->50->100%; coordinate with raj for customer updates. Set incident status to INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATING.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 1769823456: status=MITIGATING, severity=SEV2, started=1769823456, lead=jess, links=https://rwd.incidents/1769823456

raj: sending initial customer note now. Will follow up at 30m and 2h with impact summary.

maria: note for postmortem: collect stack traces, kernel source diff for fused attention, and decision timeline for disabling TRT. Also include memory usage histograms and sequence length distribution during incident window.

alex: thanks team. jess, if you need escalation to infra for node decommission, ping me and I'll wake infra lead.

jess: will do. updating incident page with latest logs and S3 dump paths. continuing monitoring. Thanks.
